title: Peloponnesian League
capsule: The Peloponnesian League was a Spartan-led alliance of city-states in the Peloponnese and central Greece, formed around 550 BCE as Sparta extended its hegemony over Corinth, Elis, and other poleis. At its apex it mobilized Greek forces to defeat Athens and its Delian League allies in the Peloponnesian War (431–404 BCE), with the Peace of Nicias (421 BCE) and Lysander's final victory ending Athenian naval supremacy. The League's coherence dissolved after Sparta's catastrophic defeat at Leuctra in 371 BCE to the Thebans under Epaminondas, and the alliance was formally ended by Philip II of Macedon's imposition of the League of Corinth in 337 BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The constituent member states are reasonably documented, but precise territorial boundaries of the alliance at any given date are not mapped in ancient sources.
